title: Adaptive granular-splitter for prefill/decode latency vs fairness tuning
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Current prefill/decode allocator uses coarse phase splitting which leads to occasional latency spikes for low-token, latency-sensitive requests and unfair resource allocation across customer tiers. This ticket proposes an adaptive granular-splitter that breaks work into micro-slices (microphases) based on predicted KV-cache reuse and attention cost heuristics, then schedules micro-slices with a utility-based fairness controller that enforces per-QoS latency targets while preserving throughput.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New splitter is behind a runtime feature flag and can be toggled per-cluster. 2) On canary workloads, p95 tail latency for latency-sensitive traces improves by >=12% vs baseline while throughput impact <=5%. 3) Observed fairness index (Gini coefficient of served tokens across QoS buckets) improves or remains equal. 4) No increase in OOM or kernel failure rate. 5) Automated e2e perf test added to CI that validates behavior under mixed workload (50% short-latency, 50% long-throughput).
design_notes:
- Micro-slice granularity: create slices based on token-span heuristics and predicted KV-cache hit probability. Default starting slice sizes: short requests=8 tokens, medium=32, long=128; splitter will adapt based on runtime feedback.
- Cost estimator: combine attention-window cost, KV cache reuse, and kernel selection hints to estimate expected kernel time for a micro-slice.
- Utility function: U = w_latency * f(latency_headroom) + w_fairness * f(fairness_deficit) + w_throughput * f(predicted_tokens/sec). We will expose w_* as tunables per deployment class.
- Arbitration: admission control reserves small fast-path slots for latency SLO requests; remaining capacity is shared using proportional fairness on utility scores.
- Safety: hard limits on micro-slice splits per-request to avoid fragmentation; default max_slices=12.
- Telemetry: emit slice-level metrics (slice_size, predicted_cost, actual_cost, kernel_hint, kv_hit_est, queue_delay) and per-request aggregated latency chain.
implementation_plan:
1) Proto implementation: splitter + cost estimator + utility arbitrator in runtime (feature-flagged). 2) Unit tests for splitter correctness and slice accounting. 3) Microbench harness to simulate mixed workloads and produce perf reports. 4) Canary rollout to non-prod clusters with traffic replay. 5) Gradual production rollout with percent-based canary and rollback hooks.
Key modules to touch: runtime/scheduler/splitter.*, runtime/telemetry/slices.*, runtime/config/flags.
PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1724 (proto splitter), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1750 (telemetry plumbing).
metrics: Monitored metrics: request_p50_ms, request_p95_ms, request_p99_ms, tokens_per_second, kernel_error_rate, slice_count_per_request, gini_fairness_index, tail_latency_by_qos. Success thresholds: p95 latency down >=12% on latency-sensitive cohort; throughput delta <=5%; gini <=0.14. We'll compare against baseline trace corpus in perf-run-2026-02.
rollout_plan:
- Stage 0: Feature flag behind 'granular_splitter' false by default.
- Stage 1 (Canary): Enable on two non-prod clusters and run traffic replay for 48h. Validate metrics and stability.
- Stage 2 (Shadow): Enable in shadow on a small subset of prod traffic (5%) and collect telemetry for 72h.
- Stage 3 (Incremental): 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback if p99 increases >10% or kernel_error_rate increases.
- Post-rollout: Run 2-week guardrail monitoring and collect customer impact signals.
Rollout owners: Marco Liu (scheduler), Priya Rao (telemetry), SRE on-call for cluster rollback.
